### Contributing guidelines - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch ### Module(s) mini.completion ### Neovim version 0.12 (!at least latest Nightly build!) ### Description

Summary

When using mini.completion on Neovim 0.10‑dev with TypeScript/Deno:

It looks as though Mini’s two‑stage pipeline never reaches the LSP stage, or completefunc is not wired up to the LSP when source_func = 'omnifunc'.

Environment

  • OS: macOS 14.5 (Apple Silicon)

  • Neovim: v0.10.0-dev-1202-g3341ab0 (built from HEAD via Homebrew --HEAD)

  • mini.nvim: v0.11.0 (lazy‑loaded, commit abc1234)

  • Language server: denols via nvim-lspconfig

  • mini.completion config

-- modules/mini.lua
local M = {}
M.cfg = {
  delay = { completion = 100, info = 100, signature = 50 },

  window = {
    info      = { height = 25, width = 100 },
    signature = { height = 25, width = 100 },
  },

  lsp_completion = {
    -- I switched this to 'omnifunc'; default is 'completefunc'
    source_func = 'omnifunc',
    auto_setup  = true,
  },

  fallback_action = '<C-n>',
  mappings = {
    force_twostep   = '<C-Space>',
    force_fallback  = '<A-Space>',
    scroll_down     = '<C-f>',
    scroll_up       = '<C-b>',
  },
}
return M

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open any *.ts file (TypeScript) with the above config.

  2. Inside a test file, declare an object and type objectName.
    Expected: popup with one field.
    Actual: no popup or only buffer words.

  3. Press <C-Space> to force two‑step completion.
    Expected: same rich list.
    Actual: buffer words again.

  4. Press <C-x><C-o>.
    Expected/Actual: full LSP‑powered list including static members – works.

Expected behaviour

  • Auto‑popup and <C-Space> should surface the same LSP candidates that <C-x><C-o> shows (static members, methods, etc.).

Actual behaviour

  • Auto‑popup / <C-Space> show only buffer keyword results, not LSP completions.

Screenshots

  1. Auto‑popup (buffer words only)

  2. <C-Space>** / force‑two‑step (buffer words only)**


  3. <C-x><C-o>** / omnifunc (✔ full LSP list)**


### Reproduction 1. **Make a Deno mono‑repo** Organize all backend & frontend packages under one git root. Keep common settings in a top‑level `deno.json` (or `deno.jsonc`). 2. **Set up ************************`mini.nvim`************************ completion** Follow the official docs for [mini.completion](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim#mini-completion) to enable LSP, snippet, and buffer sources. 3. **Add this Lua plugin spec** Put it in your Neovim plugin manager (Lazy, Packer, etc.): ```lua local theme = require('core.theme') local snippets = require('core.snippets') require('core.file-picker') local pairs = require('core.pairs') local jmp_cfg = require('core.jump') local complete = require('core.complete') return { 'echasnovski/mini.nvim', version = false, -- always track HEAD event = 'VeryLazy', dependencies = { { 's1n7ax/nvim-window-picker', lazy = false, opts = jmp_cfg.dflt_config, }, }, config = function() -------------------------------------------------- -- 1. Prerequisite module setups -------------------------------------------------- local snippetsConfig = snippets.config() pairs.setup() -------------------------------------------------- -- 2. mini.nvim modules -------------------------------------------------- require('mini.comment').setup() require('mini.completion').setup(complete.cfg) require('mini.snippets').setup(snippetsConfig) require('mini.pairs').setup(pairs.config()) require('mini.surround').setup() require('mini.basics').setup() require('mini.bracketed').setup() require('mini.bufremove').setup() require('mini.diff').setup() require('mini.files').setup() require('mini.jump').setup() require('mini.jump2d').setup() require('mini.pick').setup() require('mini.animate').setup() require('mini.base16').setup({ palette = theme }) require('mini.cursorword').setup() require('mini.icons').setup() require('mini.indentscope').setup() require('mini.notify').setup() require('mini.statusline').setup() require('mini.tabline').setup() require('mini.trailspace').setup() require('mini.fuzzy').setup() -------------------------------------------------- -- 3. Redirect vim.notify through mini.notify -------------------------------------------------- vim.notify = require('mini.notify').make_notify() end, } ``` 4. **Try it out** * Open Neovim.\* * Edit a file (TypeScript, Lua, etc.).\* * Start typing—completion should **auto‑pop** via `mini.completion` or appear with ``. 5. **Profit 🥳😜**

Thanks for the detailed issue!

I did not try to fully reproduce, as my first instinct is that it has something to do with config (and because I have easy way of reproducing if the steps follow the provided full template; the one with 'mini.deps').

As two-step execution is essentially a `<C-x><C-o>` behind some conditions, I'd guess there is some issues with setting proper 'omnifunc'. Could you please execute `:=vim.bo.omnifunc` and see what it prints? If everything is set up correctly, it should be `v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp`.

Sorry about that, ive been a programmer for a while but I've worked by myself so still getting used to GitHub lol. The printout is exactly that "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp" interesting behavior. its ONLY static members that I have noticed, other things autocomplete great. that's super weird. okay more interesting behavior. If you change the to 'omnifunc' now omnifunc complete doesn't work `````` but if you set it like this: source_func = 'completefunc', then it does. it seems that somehow the plugin might be overwriting the functionality?

> its ONLY static members that I have noticed, other things autocomplete great. that's super weird.

Can you please provide a more explicit reproduction steps, as minimal as possible? The whole file content, the exact cursor position, and which keys to press. I am not super knowledgeable with Typescript/Javascript/Deno. I just created fully contained reproduction steps and indeed see completion working just fine (I have `const a = { one: "1", };` and on next line `a.` autocompletes; just as in one of the screenshots).

A mostly note for future self.

The extra reason why this particular use case will *kind of* work with `vim.o.omnifunc = 'v:lua.vim.lsp.omnifunc'` (after pressing `<C-x><C-o>` after `.`) is because it [computes LSP boundary only based on the `item.textEdit.range`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/efd0fa55c8b1ba78692382c52a9d644fdd5488c8/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/completion.lua#L372) (which are not present in this use case's output). It will show all items (as the "base" is computed as empty string), but will autocomplete `Symbol` entry as `DataView.[Symbol]`.

The 'mini.completion' on the other hand tries to use both [`item.textEdit.range` and `item.textEdit.insert`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/01dce72f2177de6044bcab60ebb8f8e56ade0936/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1804-L1805), so it picks up the `.` as LSP's boundary.

Another difference is that `vim.lsp.omnifunc()` seems to check that all present `item.textEdit.range` agree about the final column while 'mini.completion' uses the first one (which is more performant and works fine for LSP servers with good behavior).

**Edit**: Respecting `InsertReplaceText` for LSP completion start was added in de85dec751b2a61a850f63b26df78642900fabd2 to resolve #708. So removing it is probably not an option.

Thanks for the details! 

I tried this and it seems to be working.

I'll battle test it and see if it works long term:

```
function M.apply()
  pcall(function()
    local mini_comp    = require('mini.completion')
    local default_proc = mini_comp.default_process_items

    ---@param items lsp.CompletionItem[]
    ---@param base  string
    ---@return lsp.CompletionItem[]
    local function dot_safe_process(items, base)
      local cleaned = {}

      for _, it in ipairs(items) do
        local te = it.textEdit
        local replaces_one_char =
            te and te.replace
            and (te.replace["end"].character - te.replace.start.character == 1)

        -- Skip completions that overwrite the single dot we just typed
        if not (replaces_one_char and base == ".") then
          table.insert(cleaned, it)
        end
      end

      -- Don’t treat "." as part of the prefix when filtering
      if base == "." then base = "" end

      return default_proc(cleaned, base)
    end

    -- Inject our custom processor
    mini_comp.config.lsp_completion.process_items = dot_safe_process
  end)
end
```

So even after pondering on this, I still think that this is mostly an issue with LSP server and there is nothing much 'mini.completion' can do here.

Respecting items with `InsertReplaceText` when computing LSP completion start is necessary. It can lead to weird behavior if mixed with completion items with other structure (like only having `label` present), but it feels more like a "LSP server can do better here".

> Another difference is that `vim.lsp.omnifunc()` seems to check that all present `item.textEdit.range` agree about the final column while 'mini.completion' uses the first one (which is more performant and works fine for LSP servers with good behavior).

Both ways of handling LSP start computation conflicts within same array of completion items can lead to improper start column. The question is whether falling back to keyword based computation is more robust if there is any conflict, to which I don't there is a definitive answer. As the current approach of using the first recognized LSP start is more efficient for "proper" cases (when they all are the same), I'd keep using it. But it is not a definitive decision and might be changed if there are more cases against it.

Closing as both "not really an issue with 'mini.completion'" and "nothing much more 'mini.completion' can do here". Configuring some ad-hoc `config.lsp_completion.process_items` might be the best suggestion here. Note, that this is also possible to do on language/filetype basis via [buffer-local config](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/01dce72f2177de6044bcab60ebb8f8e56ade0936/doc/mini-completion.txt#L80-L82).

Hey, I love how you work you are very methodical.

My solution seems to be working, ive tested the crap out of it and made some improvements. The only thing that I have lost is keys for objects that start with '.'

Which is really not a convention that is used at all. Do you think that would work?
